arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Sloan argued that the Eighth Amendment prohibits executing people with intellectual disabilities.
Mr. Sloan noted that the lower court relied on specific Texas legal standards.
Mr. Keller stated that the side that brought the case conceded the use of older diagnostic manuals was acceptable.
Justice Kennedy questioned whether the presented question addresses the core issues of the case.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on whether Texas courts must apply current medical standards when determining if a defendant is intellectually disabled. the side that brought the case argues Texas law ignores these standards. The state argues its legal framework remains valid.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case determines whether states must adopt current medical standards when assessing intellectual disability in death penalty cases. It defines the scope of constitutional protections for individuals facing execution. It clarifies the relationship between state law and federal constitutional mandates.
